transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess I’m here because… I’ve been having trouble staying where I’m supposed to be, like at my work station or in meetings. I don’t mean to be difficult or anything, it’s just I’ll kind of pop up or walk off before I’ve really thought about it.

My supervisor said it’s starting to be a safety issue, so… I thought I should come talk to someone before it gets worse. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you're thinking about what you're doing before you get up and walk off?

Honestly… not really. I mean, I don’t want it to sound like I’m just ignoring rules on purpose, because I’m not. It’s more like I’m at my station or in a meeting and then I’m already up or walking off before I’ve really thought it through. My supervisor said it’s becoming a safety problem, so… yeah, I guess that’s what brought me in.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through in other areas of your life, not just at work?

Yeah… I guess sometimes. I don’t mean to be rude or anything, but I’ll kind of jump into people’s conversations at work, or answer before the lead is even finished asking something.

I usually realize right after, like, “Oh, I should’ve waited,” and then people get irritated with me. I’m not trying to interrupt, it just comes out. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make it obvious, but sitting still is hard for me.

Like in certification classes or safety meetings, my foot will be bouncing the whole time, or I’ll be clicking a pen, picking at my sleeves, shifting around in the chair… and sometimes people ask me to stop. I’m not trying to be annoying, it just kind of happens. Is that what you mean?
Do you usually feel upset or anxious right before you act on impulse or get up and walk off?

I’m not sure… I don’t think it’s usually like I’m upset first, if that makes sense.

It’s more like I just do it, and then afterward I notice people looking at me or I realize I walked off. Then I get embarrassed or worried I messed up. But right before? I don’t really know that I feel anxious. I haven’t noticed that, anyway.
Do you often find yourself not paying attention to details or making careless mistakes at work or in other activities?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I try to be careful, especially at work, because I don’t want to mess anything up.

I guess I’d have to think about it more… like, I don’t know if I’d call them careless mistakes. Maybe everybody misses little things sometimes? What kind of details do you mean?
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks or projects that you start?

I’m not totally sure. I mean… I do try to finish what I start, especially if someone’s counting on me.

Sometimes I’ll start something and then it takes longer than I meant, or I kind of need reminders, but I don’t know if that’s “often” or just normal. What would count as having trouble finishing?
Do you have trouble organizing your tasks or workspace?

I don’t know… I mean, I try to keep things kind of together, especially at work. I wouldn’t want anyone thinking I’m messy or not trying.

My space can get a little all over the place sometimes, but I usually know where things are, I think. With tasks, I kind of just do what’s in front of me first. I’m not sure if that counts as trouble organizing or if that’s just how I do it.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted when you're trying to focus on something?

Yeah… I guess I do, more than I’d like to admit. At work on the line, even if I know I’m supposed to stay focused on my own station, like one beep from another machine or somebody walking by with a pallet jack can pull my eyes over, and then my whole brain kind of goes with it for a second.

I try not to let it, because I know I’m supposed to be paying attention, but it happens. Is that what you mean by easily distracted?
Do you experience these impulsive and restless behaviors at home or in your free time, not just at work?

Yeah… it’s not only at work. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m bouncing off the walls all the time, but even at home or if I’m supposed to just sit through something, I get this feeling like pressure building up in my body.

Like I need to move, or stretch, or get up and pace, or go do something right then. Same kind of thing happens if I’m standing still by the machine or sitting in training. I try to be respectful and not make it obvious, but it’s hard to just stay still. Does that make sense?
Have you always been like this, even when you were a kid?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I wasn’t trying to be difficult.

But even in elementary school, I remember being the one who couldn’t really stay in my seat. I’d talk over the teacher sometimes, or blurt things out before I was supposed to. I got notes sent home for that kind of stuff… like wandering around the room or speaking out of turn.

I guess I’ve kind of always been like this, just maybe I tried to hide it better as I got older. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have these behaviors and feelings of restlessness caused problems for you in your relationships or daily life outside of work?

Yeah… I mean, I try to keep it together, and I don’t want to blame everything on that, but it has caused problems.

Mostly at work, honestly. I’ve been written up before for safety stuff and production issues, and that scares me because I’m trying to keep the job and work toward getting certified. And… I think some coworkers don’t really want to partner with me during handoffs as much, because they’re not sure I’ll be on top of everything.

I feel bad saying that out loud. I don’t want it to sound like I don’t care, because I do care. It’s just… it’s started to affect real things, I guess.
Have you experienced these impulsive and restless behaviors consistently throughout your life, or have they varied in intensity over time?

I think it’s been pretty consistent, honestly… maybe it looks different now because I try harder to control it.

Like, even back in elementary school, I was kind of that kid who had trouble staying in my seat. I’d talk over the teacher sometimes, or blurt things out, or wander around the room, and I’d get notes sent home for it. I don’t think I was trying to be disrespectful or anything… I just had a hard time stopping myself.

So yeah, it’s been there a long time. Maybe the intensity changes depending on the situation, but it’s not really new. Is that what you mean?
Have you ever had a period in your life where you didn't experience any of these impulsive or restless behaviors for at least a few months?

Not really, no… I mean, I don’t think there’s been a few months where it just wasn’t there at all.

It’s been more of a serious problem for maybe the last year and a couple months, especially since I started trying to clean up my habits and work toward forklift and CNC certification. I wanted to be more dependable, so I noticed it more, I guess… or it mattered more.

But I don’t think I’ve had a long stretch where I was just completely calm or not impulsive. Is that answering it right?
Did these impulsive and restless behaviors start before you were 12 years old?

Yeah… yes, I think so. Even in elementary school, before I was 12, I was that kid who couldn’t really stay in my seat. I’d talk over the teacher or blurt things out, and sometimes I’d wander around the room and get notes sent home.

I don’t think I was trying to be bad or anything… it just kind of happened before I could stop myself. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often forget things you're supposed to do, like tasks or appointments?

Yeah… I do, more than I’d like to admit. I try not to make excuses for it, but I forget normal stuff all the time.

Like at work I’ll miss clocking a step on a checklist, or I’ll see a supervisor’s text and mean to answer it, then somehow I don’t. Or I’ll leave my safety glasses in my locker and not realize until I need them. It makes me feel bad because it probably looks like I just don’t care, but I really am trying. Is that the kind of forgetting you mean?
Do you often have difficulty with sustaining attention in tasks or activities?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can start out really trying, especially with stuff like inventory logs or reading the CNC training pages, because I do want to get it right.

But after a few minutes it’s like the numbers or the words kind of blur together, and then I realize I didn’t really take in what I just read. So I have to keep going back over it. I feel kind of embarrassed saying that, because I don’t want it to sound like I’m not trying. I am trying… it just doesn’t stick sometimes.
Do you experience these impulsive and restless behaviors in social situations or when you're alone, not just at work or in formal settings?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I notice it more when people point it out, like at work or places where I’m supposed to be still.

When I’m just alone, I guess I don’t really think about it as much. And socially… I don’t know, maybe I can get a little too excited or talk fast, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. What kind of things would count?
Have you ever been diagnosed with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder or been told you might have it?

No… not officially, I don’t think. Nobody’s ever sat me down and said I have that or anything.

I mean, people have kind of joked that I’m “all over the place” before, but I don’t know if that counts. I’ve never had a real evaluation for it, as far as I know. Is that okay to say?
Do you think your impulsivity and restlessness have caused more problems for you than your inattention?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to blame everything on that, but honestly the bigger issue is probably the getting up and moving before I really think.

Like, what actually brought me in was I keep leaving my station, or I’ll pop up during meetings when I’m supposed to stay put. I don’t mean it in a disrespectful way or anything, but my supervisor said it’s starting to be a safety problem because I kind of just take off before I’ve thought it through.

So… yeah, I guess the restlessness and impulsive stuff has caused more trouble than just losing focus. Is that what you mean?
